          How to use the time machine

          1. Choose something from the list, search any star name or coordinates, or click a place on the sky map.
          2. Press ▶ or drag the timeline to move through the years. Stars that are close to us slowly move; some stars change brightness; comets move within hours.
          3. Compare two dates: press Set A and Set B on the timeline, then choose Blink, Swipe or Difference (blue = brighter in A, orange = brighter in B).
          4. Since 2000 / SPHEREx only: SPHEREx started in 2025. Older NASA images (2MASS ≈2000, WISE 2010) show motion over 26 years.
          5. D1–D6 are SPHEREx's six infrared detectors, from 0.75 µm (closest to red light) to 5 µm (heat). Cold brown dwarfs only show up at the long end.

          Markers

          • Predicted position — from the star's known motion (SIMBAD) or IRSA's comet ephemeris. A guide, not a detection.
          • Measured position — where the light actually is in this image.
          • Path — where the object was and will be, year by year.

          Why do stars look like blobs?

          SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 colours, so its pixels are large (6.2″). Stars are smaller than one pixel and appear as soft dots. Use Sharp pixels to see the real pixels, and Brightness/Contrast to see faint things.

          Keys

          Space play · ←→ date · A/Z set A/B · B blink · S swipe · D difference · P movie · +− zoom · 0 whole field · T target · 1–6 detector

          About

          An independent entry for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Planet X and SPHEREx. Not an official NASA service.

          Data

          • SPHEREx spectral images, Quick Releases QR2 and QR3 (2025–2026), from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).
          • 2MASS (≈2000) and WISE (2010) images from IRSA, for the "Since 2000" view.
          • Star positions and motions from SIMBAD (CDS); comet positions from IRSA's 3I/ATLAS table.
          • Sky map: SPHEREx DR1, 2MASS and AllWISE maps from NASA/IPAC IRSA, shown with Aladin Lite (CDS software).

          Limits

          Predicted positions are guides, not detections. SPHEREx's wavelength changes across its detectors; compare brightness only between images with similar wavelength (shown for every image). 2MASS and WISE use other wavelengths and units, so compare their positions, not their brightness.
